'''Massiffs''' were [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] creatures found on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] and [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. The [[Species/Legends|species]]' original [[Planet/Legends|world]] was unknown; however, the Geonosis and Tatooine populations were by far the most numerous. [[Canine/Legends|Canine]] in appearance with an [[Armor/Legends|armored]] hide, the beasts could be domesticated and used for sentry and guard tasks. On Geonosis, possession of a massiff was a sign of authority and aristocracy. The [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosians]] and massiffs had a somewhat symbiotic relationship; in exchange for shelter, the creatures would rid the hives of pests. It was easy to tell the age of a massiff, for they grew a new pair of antlers every [[Standard year/Legends|standard year]].

==Biology and appearance==
Massiffs were [[Reptile/Legends|reptiles]]<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> that had coarse skin, large jaws, [[Tooth/Legends|toothy]] mouths, big dark [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and a line of hard spikes along their backs.<ref name="Card-SWGTCG-Massiff House Pet">{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|cardname=Massiff House Pet}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Massiff_TotG.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A pair of fighting massiffs.]]
In addition to being introduced to [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]], the massiff was domesticated by the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Researchers believe that an interstellar [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] carrying the animals crashed in one of the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Sandstorm/Legends|sandstorms]] around [[222 BBY/Legends|222 BBY]]. The resulting slaughter by the Sand People left only one survivor, while a small portion of the massiffs were kept by the attackers. Their senses being attuned to the clear conditions of Geonosis, massiffs were useless as sentries in Tatooine's constantly blowing sand. Instead, they found their niche as camp defenders, attacking any intruders on sight. The presence of massiffs was a contentious one among the Tusken clans, as many felt that they were a departure from tradition. Because of this, warring clans would often try to slay each other's pets as gestures of insult.

[[File:Massiff_AOEPII.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A view of a massiff's jagged teeth and large eyes]]
The proximity of Geonosis and Tatooine undoubtedly led to the migration of the creature from one world to another, most likely the result of careless traders introducing the animal into a new ecosphere. On Geonosis, massiffs were emblems of the Geonosian aristocracy, and domesticated massiffs were used to rid the hives of vermin. On occasion, massiffs were used in arena fighting. On Tatooine, they were similarly domesticated as camp guard animals.

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], at least [[Grizzer (massiff)/Legends|one]] massif was used by the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] for military purposes, being handled by an [[Advanced Recon Force trooper/Legends|ARF trooper]] accordingly nicknamed "[[Hound/Legends|Hound]]." He was used to track [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

==Behind the scenes==
The massiff design originated first as an [[Orray/Legends|orray]] concept. When it was deemed too vicious-looking for the simple pack animals, the massiff instead became a dog-sized lizard that was to attack [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] during a scene ultimately cut from the film.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref>

Rather than discard the work already done on the massiff, the creature was transplanted to Tatooine. The computer-generated model was used instead as a Tusken Raider guard dog, replacing a creature design originally called a [[faybo]].<ref name="DB-massiff">{{DB|creature|massiff|massiff}}</ref>
